chief_complaint: sharp tearing pain during bowel movement, blood on paper
hpi_details: A 68-year-old female presents to the clinic with sharp tearing pain during bowel movement, blood on paper. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she tore a severe internal hemorrhoid from straining during recent bouts of constipation.
concerns: She is worried that the bright red blood is the first sign of rectal cancer like her older sister was diagnosed with.
expectations: She hopes to get a prescription for a soothing numbing ointment and stool softeners to make bathroom visits tolerable.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Anal Fissure is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management for Anal Fissure emphasizes stool softeners, a high-fiber diet, and topical nitroglycerin ointment, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

teaching.one_liner: A small tear in the anoderm, usually posterior midline, causing sharp tearing pain during and after defecation with bright red blood on the paper.
red_flags: Fissure that is off the midline or not healing — consider Crohn's disease

must_ask.say: Does the sharp pain happen during or right after a bowel movement?
Does it feel like tearing or cutting?
Do you see blood on the toilet paper?
Have you been constipated or straining recently?
How long has this pain been happening?

history.answer: Whenever I have a bowel movement, I feel a sharp tearing pain down there, and I saw bright red blood on the toilet paper.
It is bright red, like fresh drops of blood. It is definitely not dark or black.
The blood only shows up when I wipe with toilet paper. It is not mixed into the stool, and it doesn't pool in the bowl.
It started about five days ago. It happens almost every time I go to the bathroom, just a couple of streaks on the paper.
It feels like a sharp, intense tearing or cutting sensation, almost like passing broken glass.
The worst pain is right as the stool passes, but then a throbbing ache lingers for about an hour afterward.
No, I haven't noticed any lump or swelling protruding from my anus, and there is no severe itching.
I often have hard stools and have to strain quite a bit on the toilet, especially over the past week.
My stool was quite hard and bulky right before this started, but it hasn't become pencil-thin and I don't feel like stool is trapped inside.
No, I do not have any stomach cramps or belly pain.
No diarrhea at all, and I have not seen any mucus or pus in my stool.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
No dizziness, fainting, or racing heartbeat when I stand up.
I have been feeling generally tired lately, but my clothes fit the same and I haven't lost weight.
No, I have no stomach burning, upper belly pain, indigestion, or vomiting.
I have never had hepatitis or liver issues, and I don't drink heavily.
No, I don't take aspirin, ibuprofen, blood thinners, or iron supplements.
No, I haven't eaten beets, blueberries, blood sausage, or anything that would color my stool.
I had a screening colonoscopy four years ago and they told me everything looked completely normal.
I have generally been healthy, with no chronic conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I am not taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, or herbal supplements.
I don't have any known allergies to medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes in my life.
I only have an occasional glass of wine with dinner, maybe once or twice a month.
I am retired and live at home with my husband.
There is no family history of colon cancer, polyps, or inflammatory bowel disease.
I thought I must have ruptured a bad hemorrhoid from straining so hard on the toilet recently.
I'm so scared that seeing blood down there means I have bowel cancer like my sister had.
I'm hoping you can give me an effective numbing cream and some stool softeners so going to the bathroom doesn't hurt so much.

exam.finding: Alert, comfortable at rest, but appears anxious regarding bowel movements.
Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, pulse 72/min, respiratory rate 14/min, temperature 36.6°C, SpO2 99% on room air.
No orthostatic hypotension; pulse and blood pressure remain stable upon standing.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor; sclerae are clear and non-icteric.
Abdomen is flat and symmetric, with no scars or visible masses.
Normal active bowel sounds heard in all four quadrants; no bruits.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended without palpable masses or organomegaly.
No rebound tenderness or signs of peritoneal irritation.
Gently separating the buttocks reveals a small, fresh longitudinal tear in the posterior midline anoderm; no external hemorrhoids or fistula openings.
Marked anal sphincter spasm and severe tenderness at the posterior midline; no palpable rectal mass, with a speck of bright red blood on the examining glove.
